watch.en: Heat the sugar until it melts and turns a deep brown, from about 170 °C; have cold water ready to stop the browning.
watch.de: Den Zucker erhitzen, bis er schmilzt und tiefbraun wird, ab etwa 170 °C; kaltes Wasser bereitstellen, um das Bräunen zu stoppen.

why.en: Heat acting on melting sugar changes it into a deep brown colour with new flavours. The longer it cooks, the less sweet and the more bitter it gets, and once it browns it goes on by itself.
why.de: Hitze verwandelt schmelzenden Zucker in eine tiefbraune Masse mit neuen Aromen. Je länger er gart, desto weniger süß und desto bitterer wird er, und hat das Bräunen einmal begonnen, geht es von selbst weiter.

sources.title: Understanding Ingredients for the Canadian Baker (BCcampus)
sources.sentence: At high temperatures, the chemical changes associated with melting sugars result in a deep brown colour and new flavours.

sources.title: Understanding Ingredients for the Canadian Baker (BCcampus)
sources.sentence: Caramelization results from the action of heat on sugars.

sources.title: McGee on Food and Cooking (Harold McGee), Hodder & Stoughton 2004
sources.place: chapter Sugars, Chocolate, and Confectionery, Caramelization - Making Caramel, p. 657
sources.sentence: It’s helpful to have a bowl of cold water ready to cool the pan down as soon as the caramel is done.

sources.title: McGee on Food and Cooking (Harold McGee), Hodder & Stoughton 2004
sources.place: chapter Sugars, Chocolate, and Confectionery, Caramelization, p. 656
sources.sentence: The more the sugar is cooked, the less sugar and sweetness remain, and the darker and more bitter it gets.
